title: Spinaci Ripassati
subtitle: Sauteed spinach with garlic, olive oil, and chilli
excerpt: Spinaci ripassati is wilted spinach cooked a second time in olive oil with garlic and chilli. The spinach is blanched first, squeezed dry, then tossed in a hot pan with garlic and chilli until it has absorbed the oil and the garlic is fragrant. It takes 10 minutes and goes with almost anything.
sourceNotes: Spinaci ripassati (literally 'spinach passed again' in the pan) is the standard Italian technique for cooking leafy greens: blanch, squeeze dry, then fry briefly in well-seasoned oil. The method is used across Italy for spinach, chard, cavolo nero, and other greens. It appears throughout Italian regional cooking and is one of the most common vegetable preparations in Italian home kitchens.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Blanch and squeeze the spinach up to 24 hours ahead. Keep in the fridge. The final fry takes 3 minutes.

content.text: Spinaci ripassati is the Italian way to cook spinach: blanch it briefly to wilt it, squeeze out the water firmly, then fry it a second time in good olive oil with garlic and chilli. The squeezing is the step most people skip and the step that makes the difference. Watery spinach fried in a pan steams rather than fries and loses flavour. Dry squeezed spinach absorbs the garlicky oil and tastes entirely different.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add the spinach and blanch for 60 to 90 seconds until wilted. Drain in a colander and run cold water over it to stop the cooking.
Take the spinach in handfuls and squeeze hard to remove as much water as possible. It should feel damp but not wet. Roughly chop it if the leaves are large.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes if using. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the spinach. Toss it in the pan for 2 to 3 minutes until heated through and well coated in the garlic oil. Season with salt. Taste and adjust.

The ripassata method is used across Italy for any leafy green: spinach, chard, cavolo nero, broccoli raab. It is the standard Italian way to finish cooked vegetables rather than simply boiling or steaming them. The second pass in the pan with garlic and oil is where the flavour is built. In Rome, spinaci ripassati is a classic contorno (side dish) served alongside meat or fish.
